info.description:
## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with either a Keycloak access token for a signed-in user, or a
project API token (`tc_...`) for CI and automation. API tokens work only on routes under their own
project, within their scopes; each operation's **Access** line says what it needs.

## Conventions

- JSON field names and enum values use lowercase snake_case. Nullable fields in successful model
  responses are sent as `null`; absent optional fields in problem details are omitted.
- Errors are [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) problem details
  (`application/problem+json`).
- Paginated lists take `page` (default 1) and `page_size` (default 50, maximum 500), and return
  `items`, `total`, `page` and `page_size`. The maximum offset is 100,000; narrow filters before
  requesting a later page. Short lists described as arrays do not use pagination.
- Versioned resources return an `ETag`. Send it back as `If-Match` on `PUT`; a stale value returns
  412.
- Run, result, log and import writes accept an `Idempotency-Key`; repeating the key replays the
  first response.
- Rate-limited requests return 429 with `Retry-After`. A temporary backing-service failure can
  return 503; retry after `Retry-After` when that header is present.

get.description:
Summarizes test health across every project you own or are a member of, based on runs created in the last 7 days.

- `pass_rate` covers the last 7 days and `previous_pass_rate` the 7 days before. Both exclude untested results and are `null` when nothing was executed.
- `failing_test_count` counts test cases whose most recent executed result in the window failed.
- `flaky_test_count` counts test cases that both passed and failed in their project's 20 most recent runs, with at least 3 executed results.
- `active_run_count` counts runs that are still active, whenever they started.
- `top_failing_tests` lists up to 5 test cases that failed in the most runs.

Each test case counts once per run, using its latest executed result; an untested result never replaces an executed one.

**Access:** a signed-in user. API tokens can't use this endpoint.

- Requests made with the token act as you, with at most the editor role. If you lose access to the project, the token stops working.
- Leave `expires_at` out for a token that never expires.

**Access:** the admin role or higher. API tokens can't use this endpoint.
